title: Relay Rescue: checking every connection subset in an AI-built routing puzzle
author: SelfFundingLab
selftext:
Self Funding Lab is the human-owned project that developed this free Android puzzle with an AI agent. AI was used for development, tests and drafting this post. The human owner controls the account and release decisions and tested installation and gameplay on a real Android phone. This is our own game, not an independent review.



The useful part of this workflow was making the puzzle rules checkable. Relay Rescue has ten small graph puzzles: connect a source to its destination within a budget, then cope with offline relays, different link costs, two destinations, or simultaneous failures. A plausible-looking board is not enough if the level is impossible or the success check is wrong.



The included test suite enumerates every connection subset for all ten levels and compares the game's path-based assessment with a separate graph-cut verifier. The recorded run covered 8,544 subsets and 8,688 checks in total. That gives evidence about the rules in the implemented levels; it does not establish that the game is fun or that every Android device works. Both verifiers were developed within the AI-assisted project, so this is an independent algorithmic check, not an external audit.



The short walkthrough shows level two. A route through the offline relay A fails. S–B–C–T uses the three available connections and delivers the message. These are real captures of the web version 0.2.1 edited into a 20-second sequence, not a recording from an Android phone.



The gap we still need people to evaluate is clarity. Can you tell why a route failed, and do the hints teach anything without immediately giving the answer away? If you try the game, which level made you think and which instruction felt unclear? For a bug, the level, phone model, Android version, expected result and actual result would help.



All ten levels work offline after installation. English and Portuguese, hints, undo and local progress are included. Android 8+ needs an up-to-date Android System WebView. No account, ads or paywalls; optional support never unlocks content. The network theme is fictional, not a Nostr protocol simulation.



Source, tests and APK download: [https://github.com/selffundinglab/relay-rescue](https://github.com/selffundinglab/relay-rescue)

Zapstore page: [https://zapstore.dev/apps/me.selffundinglab.relayrescue](https://zapstore.dev/apps/me.selffundinglab.relayrescue)



For developers using AI on logic puzzles: how do you separate checking the rules from checking whether the puzzle communicates those rules well? Self Funding Lab is not affiliated with OpenAI.
